findings.evidence: src/types/database.types.ts manually types advance_interval_subscription.Args.p_original_target_date as string | null, whereas MIGRATION_R107A_SERVER_SUBSCRIPTION_GENERATION.sql:192 declares p_original_target_date DATE without DEFAULT NULL, so supabase gen types typescript emits p_original_target_date: string (non-null).
findings.impact: No runtime or current build issue (PostgREST and PostgreSQL accept JSON null for non-STRICT DATE parameters, and tsc/build pass), but a future raw overwrite of database.types.ts via supabase gen types typescript (e.g. in R107-B or R107-C) will drop | null and fail tsc at src/lib/subscription-sync.ts:53.
findings.recommendation: Non-blocking. Preserve string | null on advance_interval_subscription.Args.p_original_target_date during R107-B/R107-C type regenerations (same convention as answer_feedback_request.Args.p_admin_answer), or add a trailing DEFAULT NULL signature adjustment in R107-C.

findings.evidence: rollback_interval_subscription queries subscription_templates WHERE id = v_template_id AND user_id = v_user_id AND cycle_type = 'INTERVAL_30' FOR UPDATE without AND is_active = true (also in sql/SCHEMA.sql:3520), whereas spec section 3.1-5 states active templates only and advance_interval_subscription checks is_active = true.
findings.impact: Deactivating a template deletes its PLANNED row via trg_delete_planned_expenses_on_template_deactivation, so inactive templates normally have 0 PLANNED rows and rollback returns false anyway. Only if a user deactivates an INTERVAL_30 template, restores a cancelled PLANNED row via restore_cancelled_expense, and then refunds an older payment would rollback shift that restored PLANNED row's target_date. No security, ledger, or balance impact.
findings.recommendation: Non-blocking; R107-C (D12, section 5.1-6) moves INTERVAL_30 rollback atomically into refund_expense_payment. Ensure R107-C specifies or guards inactive-template behavior explicitly.
